blocks.content: Citizens are full members of the Indian State and owe allegiance to it, enjoying all civil and political rights.

rows: Full access to all civil and political rights (including Art 15, 16, 19, 29, 30)
Eligible for all public and Constitutional offices
Enjoy basic fundamental civil rights (e.g., Art 14, 20, 21), but no political rights
Enjoy basic civil rights subject to national security restrictions; no political rights
Not protected against arrest and detention

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Citizenship represents full and equal membership of the Indian State, conferring both civil and political rights.
The Constitution creates a single citizenship for the entire nation to promote national integration and uniformity.
Foreigners or aliens are categorized into friendly aliens and enemy aliens based on diplomatic relations.
Certain Constitutional posts (such as President, Vice-President, Judges of Supreme Court and High Courts, Governor, and Attorney General) are reserved exclusively for Indian citizens.
Both naturalized citizens and citizens by birth are eligible for the office of the President in India, unlike in the USA where only natural-born citizens are eligible.
Fundamental Rights under Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30 are exclusive to Indian citizens and denied to foreigners.
Enemy aliens do not enjoy protection against arrest and detention provided under Article 22 of the Constitution.
Unlike the United States of America, India allows both a citizen by birth as well as a naturalised citizen to hold the office of President.
